### Historical audit

**Source:** S0058, original file `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/quota_restored_20261103/retired/results/r1/sceneevolve_cli/C2/test/commons_16007442/trajectory.jsonl`. Offsets below are character ranges within the cited JSONL line.

| Evidence | Observation and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Student `model_request`, line 1 [0,9984) | The requested goal was to reconstruct an indoor photograph with separate editable objects, appropriate materials, camera and lighting. The prompt requested a visible-image specification, a complete program, source checks and subsequent render comparison. These are instructions, not evidence of completed work. The reference image is named but its contents are not visible in this audit. |
| Student `codex_session`, line 2 [0,2629) | One fresh, read-only CLI session was started with the image supplied. It reported failure, exit code 1, and zero tool calls. No autonomous tool exploration is recorded. |
| Student `model_error`, line 3 [0,550); `scene_error`, line 4 [0,1614) | The student process exited 1 while the policy was awaiting a model response. The trace points to a stderr log, but does not contain its contents; the underlying cause is unknown. |

**Outcome:** Technical interruption, not a demonstrated algorithmic or geometric failure. No student program, scene modification, successful build, render, visual validation, score or final selection is recorded. Thus the record does not establish an empty patch or partial correctness, and it cannot verify multiple objects, materials or textures, part connections, pose, camera, lighting, or render quality.

**Teacher involvement:** No teacher message, detection, diagnosis, proposed update or execution appears in this student trajectory. There is consequently no evidence of teacher receipt or adoption.

**Lessons and uncertainty:** A transferable operational lesson is to distinguish process failure from reconstruction quality and inspect the cited stderr when it is available. The task-specific unresolved question is whether a reconstruction would have matched this particular photograph; neither the image contents nor an output render is provided here. The reason for the CLI exit remains an open hypothesis, not a diagnosis.
